subtype: Approach: negotiating by swapping what each values [Thinking]
passage: In the front room of their house in the small town, Mohit had a plan for Saturday morning: the family computer, a new game and nobody bothering him. But his sister Waheeda wanted the same computer on Sunday for her science project. "I need it more," said Mohit. "So do I," said Waheeda. Then Mohit thought. "What matters to me is Saturday morning, when my friends are online. What matters to you is a long stretch to finish the project." "Sunday afternoon," said Waheeda. "Then we swap: Saturday morning for me, Sunday for you." They shook hands, and neither of them lost.

qa.q: What did Waheeda want the computer for?
qa.a: Waheeda wanted the computer for her science project.

qa.q: What did Mohit realise, and how did he feel once he saw what mattered to each of them?
qa.a: Mohit realised Saturday morning mattered to him and a long Sunday stretch mattered to Waheeda, and he seemed calmer, moving from "I need it more" to offering a swap.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Mohit and Waheeda use, and why?
qa.a: They could split the time on one day into fixed halves with a timer. Either way, each gets some of what matters most to them.

qa.q: How might Waheeda see the swap?
qa.a: Waheeda agreed to Sunday afternoon and shook hands, so Waheeda probably feels the swap gave what the project needed and that Mohit listened.

grounding: A boy wants the computer on Saturday morning for a game and his sister wants it on Sunday for a project, so they swap to give each the time that matters.

subtype: Approach: negotiating by swapping what each values [Thinking]
passage: On Friday night in their small house in Busan, Jin and his sister Dalia started the usual fight over the family computer. "I need Saturday morning," Jin said. "The online game tournament is at ten." "And I need the whole weekend for my science poster." Their mother kept chopping vegetables. Jin stopped. "Wait. When do you actually need it most?" Dalia thought. "Sunday. That's when the library pictures come back." "And I only need Saturday morning." He grinned. "So I take Saturday till twelve, and you take all of Sunday." Dalia narrowed her eyes, then held out her hand. "Deal. But Saturday afternoon's mine too." "Deal."

qa.q: What time is Jin's online game tournament?
qa.a: It is at ten on Saturday.

qa.q: How did Dalia feel when she narrowed her eyes at Jin's offer?
qa.a: She was cautious and a little suspicious, checking the deal was really fair before agreeing.

qa.q: What else could they do if both needed the same morning?
qa.a: They could split that morning by the clock or ask their mother to help decide, so neither loses everything.

qa.q: How does the swap look to their mother?
qa.a: Their mother hears the fight end on its own, and is probably relieved she didn't have to step in.

grounding: It shows siblings trading computer time so each gets the time that matters most to them.

subtype: Approach: negotiating by swapping what each values [Thinking]
passage: The community centre near their home had one free computer for families, booked by the weekend. At the front desk on Friday, Karthik and his sister Sabina both reached for the pen. "I want Saturday morning," Karthik said. "There's a chess match online." "I need the weekend for my history project," said Sabina. The volunteer waited. Karthik thought aloud. "Do you need Saturday?" "Not really. My printouts come Sunday." "Then give me Saturday morning. You get all of Sunday. That way we both get the part we care about." Sabina wrote their names in the book. The volunteer smiled. "Easiest booking all week."

qa.q: What did Karthik want the computer for on Saturday morning?
qa.a: He wanted it for an online chess match.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel when he thought aloud about the booking?
qa.a: He felt calm and curious, trying to find a deal that worked for both instead of fighting.

qa.q: What else could the siblings do if the centre only allowed one slot per family?
qa.a: They could share the one slot, with Karthik playing first and Sabina working after, since each needs only part of the time.

qa.q: How does the booking look to the volunteer?
qa.a: The volunteer is pleased and amused, calling it the easiest booking all week.

grounding: It shows two siblings swapping computer time so each gets the time they value most.
